name: 45-Degree Back Extension with Barbell
description: A weighted hyperextension exercise performed in the 45-degree back extension machine with a barbell held behind the head or at the chest. Adding barbell weight significantly increases the posterior chain loading, developing the glutes, hamstrings, and erector spinae simultaneously.

execution.starting_position: Position yourself in the 45-degree hyperextension bench with the pad across the hips. Hold a barbell plate at chest or a barbell behind the neck.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the hyperextension bench correctly. Load a barbell held at chest height or position a plate at the chest.
steps: Step 1: Lower the torso forward into full hip flexion, maintaining a neutral spine.
Step 2: Drive the hips into the pad and extend the torso upward using glute and hamstring strength.
Step 3: Extend to a neutral spine position at the top — do not hyperextend the lumbar.
Step 4: Lower back down under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent. Exhale on the extension.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the top
Using momentum to swing the torso up
safety_considerations: Stop the ascent at a neutral spine position, not beyond it
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip flexion at the bottom. Neutral spine at the top — not hyperextended.
coaching_cues: Drive through the hips, not the lower back
Stop when the body is in a straight line
